newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Wilson&Horton NZ Herald raises circulation.
newsitem.headline: Wilson&Horton NZ Herald raises circulation.

text.p: Wilson and Horton Ltd's New Zealand Herald has lifted its circulation after a static two years, a spokesman for the company said on Monday.
In the six months to March, circulation rose by 2,696 over the same year-ago period to 229,398.
Average issue readership was up by 10,000 to 550,000, the Herald said on Saturday.
The paper said the increase was a reflection of changes to the Herald, Wilson and Horton's flagship and New Zealand's largest circulating daily newspaper.
Executives at Wilson and Horton, which is 85 percent-owned by Tony O'Reilly's Independent Newspapers Ltd, have said the paper will go through more enhancements.

Wilson and Horton had in the past foreshadowed an improvement. The Herald has in recent years been in the circulation doldrums, despite sharp population increases in its target area, Auckland, where it is the only major daily.
Some analysts had expected a little weakness in the current quarter but Paul Richardson, media analyst at SBC Warburg, said he expected the Herald's position to remain solid.
Pagination, or the number of pages per issue, had been very strong, indicating strength in ad volumes, he said.
"The overall content of the paper, in terms of advertising, still seems to be very high, so I'm inclined to conclude that things look pretty good there," he said.
Wilson and Horton shares traded today at NZ$11.65, down five cents.
